To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the correlation scale of magnetic fields in collisionless shocks grows as the shock evolution time, λ(t)=ct (see Fig. 2); (2) this growth is due to the interaction of current filaments (see Fig.3); (3) the field growth leads to an inefficient dissipation of magnetic energy (see Figs. 4 and 5); (4) this result is confirmed by numerical PIC simulations (see Fig.1).

the correlation scale of magnetic fields generated in collisionless astrophysical shocks grows with time nearly as the light-crossing time, λ ∼ ct, and that the magnetic field dissipation in this regime is inefficient.
the magnetic field correlation length in the region far from the shock grows nearly linearly with time, λ(t)=ct, and that the growth is due to the interaction between current filaments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-time evolution (i.e. the evolution after the shock has passed) of the magnetic field generated by a relativistic collisionless shock.
a fundamental problem of plasma astrophysics, namely, the structure and the evolution of magnetic fields at relativistic collisionless shocks.
the long-time evolution and dissipation of magnetic fields at collisionless relativistic shocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field structure is determined by the shock structure, and the shock structure is determined by a combination of the upstream plasma conditions and the field structure.
the magnetic field in the region far behind the collisionless shock grows in a self-similar way as the light crossing distance.
the field correlation length grows with time, but the rate of this growth depends on the shock parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic field correlation scale in a relativistic shock increases with the distance from the shock front, thus making the field dissipation inefficient.
the field correlation length is not growing as the shock front thickness, but rather as the shock front distance from the upstream boundary.
the long-time evolution (i.e. after the shock has reached the asymptotic state) of magnetic fields generated at relativistic collisionless shocks is dominated by the filamentation instability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic fields in relativistic collisionless shocks are not diffusively decaying in time, but rather are growing in scale, which makes the field diffusion inefficient.
in collisionless relativistic shocks the magnetic field correlation length in the downstream region grows as λ ∼ ct, which is a very important property of such shocks.
the magnetic field correlation scale in collisionless shocks is growing in time, and this makes the diffusive field decay inefficient, at least for a long time.
